item.title: Tyler Herro's three-words sums up status with ex-teammate Bam Adebayo for first game since punching incident
item.description: Tyler Herro says he hasn't talked to Bam Adebayo as the Miami Heat host the Bucks in their first meeting since the reported Summer League altercation.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Heat welcomed the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night in a matchup that might otherwise blend into the early-season NBA schedule.

But a summer feud involving a former Heat player and one of Miami’s current stars has added an unexpected layer of intrigue to the matchup. In July, tensions between Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro reportedly boiled over in Las Vegas.

Since the dispute between the two NBA stars, questions have lingered over whether Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro had repaired their relationship or whether tensions remained.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Wednesday marked the first time the two players faced each other since the incident, and Herro was noncommittal when asked about the state of their relationship.

HEAT VS. BUCKS BEST BETS: GIANNIS GETS HIS FIRST SHOT AT MILWAUKEE

"I'm not sure. I haven't talked to him," Herro told reporters Wednesday.

Adebayo and Herro were involved in a physical altercation at an NBA Summer League practice facility, during which the Heat center allegedly struck the Milwaukee Bucks guard in the head area.

A blockbuster deal over this past offseason sent Giannis Antetokounmpo to Miami and Herro to Milwaukee, ending his time as Adebayo’s Heat teammate.

MIAMI HEAT UNVEIL VICE CITY COURT FOR 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED CLASH WITH MILWAUKEE BUCKS

Herro reflected on his time sharing a locker room with Adebayo, and praised the three-time All-Star's skillset. "Obviously I spent a lot of time with Bam. I admire his game. He's a great player. Can do everything on the floor, guard 1-5. He's gifted offensively."

Sources told ESPN that Adebayo initially confronted Herro over alleged social media comments criticizing his defense. Screenshots circulated online purportedly showed Herro questioning Adebayo’s defensive prowess in an Instagram direct message with a fan.

Adebayo agreed to a three-year, $166 million extension with Miami in June 2024. The alleged DM also appeared to question whether his nightly defensive effort justified a salary approaching $60 million.

Miami entered Wednesday night with an 8-6 record, while Milwaukee had won just once this season.

item.title: Patrick McEnroe joins Rep Tim Walberg to back Team USA Act capping foreign college athletes at 20% of rosters
item.description: Outside the U.S. Capitol, Patrick McEnroe backed the TEAM USA Act, citing nearly 70% foreign Division I tennis rosters as U.S. taxpayers fund Olympians.
item.content:encoded:
Outside the U.S. Capitol on Wednesday, International Tennis Hall of Fame President Patrick McEnroe backed the TEAM USA Act, calling for a 20% cap on international recruits to safeguard college spots for American kids.

Speaking with OutKick after a joint press conference with House Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg, McEnroe warned that foreign recruits hold nearly 70 percent of Division I tennis spots while U.S. taxpayers train hundreds of rival Olympians.

According to House Education and Workforce Committee data, the number of international athletes receiving college scholarships has nearly tripled since 2001, surging from roughly 8,945 to about 25,000 today.

PATRICK MCENROE ON U.S. OPEN WEED SMELL, TRANS ATHLETES, FOREIGN RECRUITS RESHAPING COLLEGE TENNIS

Without roster limits, college programs have turned into feeders for overseas pros, and only a strict cap can save spots for young Americans.

"Well, I think there is a good chance that we can push this through, which would limit the amount of international athletes in our collegiate system to 20%, which I think is quite fair," McEnroe told OutKick.

During Wednesday's press conference, Chairman Walberg pressed the urgency of his bill, formally titled the Training and Education for American Members in University Sports and Athletics Act (H.R. 10351).

McEnroe, who played college tennis at Stanford University in the 1980s, welcomes international competition, but noted that foreign enrollment on varsity rosters has climbed over the past 15 years, crowding American-born players out of U.S. universities.

"The numbers are stratospheric," McEnroe stated.

"I mean, it is closing in on 70% for Division I tennis players. Both male and female are in the mid-60s at the moment, and it is continuing to rise. And you are seeing it in other sports as well. Men's soccer is well over 50% now, and many rosters are pretty much 100% international athletes.

I’M A COLLEGE ATHLETE. THE SYSTEM THAT GAVE ME MY DREAM IS STARTING TO BREAK

"I do not think that is good for the ecosystem of youth sports."

Coaches have privately told McEnroe they welcome a cap to break the cycle, though few will risk their jobs by speaking out. Across college athletics, whether a football coach earns $15 million or a tennis coach makes $150, 000, athletic departments demand immediate wins, and job survival pushes programs toward older overseas talent.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"When you see your big rival down the block getting the best players they can from Europe, well, you are going to say you have got to stay in the game, so you are going to do the same thing," McEnroe explained.

"So in no way do I blame the coaches nor the athletes who are just looking for the opportunity, whether they come from Serbia, England, or Tennessee. But the kids in our country are losing opportunities. That is just the bottom line."

That recruiting arms race is hollowing out American youth sports.

A homegrown player who easily earned a spot on a top 50 tennis roster a decade ago is now shut out, leaving parents of 12- to 14-year-old prospects questioning the steep costs and years of sacrifice required for elite junior training when scholarships go to imported semi-professionals.

Rebuilding that domestic pipeline, McEnroe argued, starts with giving coaches clear guardrails.

"I think they would like to have a choice where they can get two players on their team that are international, and the rest we can make up with American kids," he noted.

SENATE MOVES TO REIN IN COLLEGE SPORTS 'WILD WEST' WITH SWEEPING NEW RULES FOR PLAYERS, SCHOOLS

"Last time I checked, the college system in sports was not supposed to be professional. I realize we sort of lost the plot there when it comes to football and basketball, but all the Olympic sports should just be training grounds for young kids and places where you can dream, have a goal, accomplish that goal, and get an education."

At Wednesday's press conference, Walberg spotlighted that paradox using the Paris Olympic Games.

While 65% of Team USA athletes had ties to NCAA athletics, only 385 of the 1,036 NCAA Olympians in Paris represented the United States, with the remaining 63% competing for foreign nations.

In effect, U.S. universities backed by state and federal tax dollars are funding the training of athletes who later compete against America on the Olympic stage. McEnroe and Walberg argue foreign governments should fund their own Olympic programs rather than relying on American taxpayers.

Under the TEAM USA Act, a uniform 20 percent cap would apply across every collegiate sport, limiting a 10-player college tennis roster to two international spots. Holding every school and coach to one rule would halt the arms race while preserving most roster spots for American athletes.

Passing the bill requires bipartisan support in the House and Senate, where Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH) introduced companion legislation. Alongside Walberg, McEnroe briefed lawmakers on the roster data, warning that many in Washington remain unaware of how dramatically college sports have shifted.

Without congressional action, McEnroe cautions, opportunities for American families will keep shrinking.

At stake is the future of the 99 percent of college athletes who never turn pro, and whether higher education preserves varsity sports as an avenue for education, character, and upward mobility.

"This is the American collegiate system, right? It is not international. It is not a professional sport," McEnroe told OutKick.

"College sports was started, and has given so many people the opportunity, because of what it is supposed to do, which is help people get an education, better their lives, and be useful members of society. That is why I am here, and that is what I am trying to help and protect."

item.title: Wife and daughter arrested after DNA IDs man whose severed head was found in trash bag
item.description: Mary Fitzmaurice allegedly kept collecting her father's Social Security and pension benefits after his death, telling relatives he was still alive.
item.content:encoded:
A California woman and her daughter were arrested more than four years after a woman walking her dog found a man's severed head in a trash bag, authorities said.

The Placer County Sheriff’s Office identified the man as Paul Wesley Fitzmaurice Jr., 73, who had never been reported missing. Authorities said his wife and daughter had told relatives the victim was still alive.

His daughter, 45-year-old Mary Fitzmaurice, and his wife, 75-year-old Georgia "Gwenn" Fitzmaurice, were booked into the South Placer Jail on Tuesday, officials said in a news release. 

Mary was booked on suspicion of murder and Gwenn on suspicion of being an accessory.

DNA BREAKTHROUGH LEADS TO ARREST IN GRISLY 33-YEAR-OLD COLD CASE INVESTIGATORS NEVER GAVE UP ON

The women "kept up the facade to family and friends that Paul was still alive," Placer County Sheriff Wayne Woo said at a news conference Wednesday. He said they continued receiving Fitzmaurice’s Social Security benefits and California public pension after his death.

Woo said the women told some of Fitzmaurice’s estranged relatives "he was being a recluse, and he would disappear for days at a time." 

They claimed he "would come back to the house every week or so and stay for a couple of days," Woo said.

In its news release, the sheriff’s office alleged Mary killed her father and the two women "conspired to dispose of his remains."

At Wednesday’s news conference, Placer County District Attorney Morgan Gire said prosecutors expected to file a murder charge against Mary Fitzmaurice by the end of the day and were weighing additional charges related to the killing and the collection of Fitzmaurice’s benefits.

Asked whether money was a motive, Woo said, "There’s still a lot of investigative work to be done, and I would be speculating on motive at this point."

NEW CALIFORNIA LAW EXPANDS DNA TOOLS FOR MISSING PERSONS INVESTIGATIONS

The dog walker found the bag on Sept. 28, 2022, in the Todd Valley area of Foresthill while the Mosquito Fire was burning nearby. Woo said the discovery drew little attention at the time.

"The people that didn’t forget about this case is the residents of Foresthill and our cold case detectives," Woo said.

The remains were too decomposed for investigators to identify the man. Forensic experts at California State University, Chico, helped produce an artist’s rendering, but it yielded no match in missing-person cases. A search of the national law enforcement DNA database also came up empty.

In January 2024, detectives sent a DNA sample to Othram Labs, which used forensic genetic genealogy to find possible distant relatives. With the FBI’s help, investigators traced the family tree and obtained a DNA sample from an out-of-state relative that helped confirm Fitzmaurice’s identity.

GIRL KNOWN AS 'CHELSEA JANE DOE' ID'D 26 YEARS AFTER MUTILATED BODY FOUND HUNDREDS OF MILES FROM HOME STATE

Othram said in a news release that Fitzmaurice’s identification marked the 94th publicly announced case in California in which investigators used its technology to identify someone.

The sheriff’s office said in its release that investigators believe Mary killed her father at the family’s Citrus Heights home, which detectives searched Tuesday with help from the FBI. 

When asked at the briefing where Fitzmaurice was killed, Woo said, "With evidence that we gathered and collected yesterday, we’ll hopefully determine that."

Woo said the rest of Fitzmaurice’s remains have yet to be found. 

"We did not find any remains at the residence yesterday," he said.

item.title: Muslims poised to outnumber Christians globally by 2035 amid demographic shifts
item.description: Pew Research Center study projects Muslims will outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035, driven by higher fertility rates and younger populations.
item.content:encoded:
People practicing the Islamic faith are poised to outnumber Christians globally by 2035, becoming the world's largest religion, according to a new study released by the Pew Research Center.

The detailed report attributes the shift primarily to higher fertility rates and younger populations among Muslims, who are growing at a faster rate than other major faiths.

"Around the world, we find that Muslims tend to have more children than non-Muslims, [and] they tend to be younger as a result of having more children in the past," Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett told Fox News Digital.

WHY PEOPLE REALLY STOPPED HAVING KIDS: NEW STUDY UNCOVERS THE SURPRISING REASONS FAMILIES ARE SHRINKING

Muslims have the highest fertility rate at 3.1 children per woman, followed by Christians at 2.5, according to the study. Between 2020 and 2025, Muslim women gave birth to 252 million babies, more than women of any other religion and compared to 208 million born to Christian mothers.

If trends continue, the United States will also undergo a major religious shift. While Christians currently account for roughly 62% to 64% of U. S. adults, that share is expected to fall below 50% by 2065.

POLL FINDS SHARP RISE IN YOUNG MEN CALLING RELIGION 'VERY IMPORTANT'

By 2070, Christians are projected to make up less than half of the U. S. population, while religiously unaffiliated individuals, known as "nones," will rise to about 41%.

"The Muslim population in the U. S. is growing faster than the Christian population, but Christians vastly outnumber Muslims in the U. S., and that's not going to change," Hackett said.

By 2070, the Muslim population in the U. S. is expected to increase to nearly 4%, making Muslims the third-largest group in the country behind Christians and the religiously unaffiliated, surpassing the U.S. Jewish population.

Globally, the demographic center of major faiths is also moving. By 2070, Pakistan is projected to have the largest Muslim population, followed by India, Nigeria and Indonesia, which currently has the largest Muslim population of any country.

POPE LEO XIV TO VISIT FASTEST-GROWING CATHOLIC CONTINENT DURING 4-NATION AFRICA TRIP

Meanwhile, the presence of Christianity is shifting southward. By 2070, more than half of the world's Christians will live in sub-Saharan Africa, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo is projected to surpass the U.S. as the country with the single greatest number of Christians.

A century ago, most of the world's Christians lived in Europe, Hackett noted. However, Europe's population is now growing slowly and expected to shrink in the coming decades, while Africa's population expands rapidly.

"Europe's population has been growing slowly, and Africa's population has been growing very quickly," Hackett said. "In the coming decades, Europe's population is expected to shrink, [while] Africa's population is going to expand a lot."

Other religious demographics are shifting as well. The global Jewish population is expected to become increasingly concentrated, with 62% living in Israel by 2070, up from 46% in 2020.

AGE OF FIRST-TIME MOTHERS HITS RECORD HIGH IN BLUE STATES AS BIRTH RATES KEEP FALLING

In addition, the global Muslim population is projected to exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, compared to just under 3 billion Christians, according to Pew.

Overall, Muslims and Christians are the only major religious groups projected to keep pace with the world's overall population growth, which is expected to increase by 29% between 2020 and 2070. Christians are projected to grow by 30% and Muslims by 80%.

GEN Z FLOCKING TO CATHOLIC CHURCHES IN NYC FOR YOUTH GROUPS, SOCIAL EVENTS AMID CONVERSION BOOM

Beyond organized religions, many countries continue to see a surge in "nones," those with no religious affiliation, atheists or agnostics.

While China holds a massive proportion of the world's religiously unaffiliated, its population decline will offset growth elsewhere, Hackett said. Excluding China, the global population of "nones" is projected to grow by more than 180 million by 2070.

The religiously unaffiliated already account for a majority of the population in 10 countries, including the Czech Republic, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Uruguay and Vietnam.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Bucket list vacation destination just got a lot tougher for Americans to reach
item.description: U.S. airlines are cutting seats to popular vacation destination Costa Rica this winter, with January capacity down 12.5%, and San José hit harder than Liberia as airfares climb.
item.content:encoded:
American travelers heading to a popular vacation getaway could face fewer flight options and higher airfares during the busy winter vacation season.

Airlines are scheduling fewer flights and offering fewer seats from the U.S. to Costa Rica in December and January compared with last year, according to flight schedule data from Cirium, an aviation analytics company that tracks airline operations worldwide. 

The drop is expected to be especially noticeable after the holidays. In January, the number of available seats from the U.S. to Costa Rica is scheduled to fall 12.5% compared to a year earlier.

BUDGET AIRLINE EXPANDS ITS FOOTPRINT WITH 11 NEW TROPICAL FLIGHT ROUTES BEGINNING IN NOVEMBER

San José appears to be taking a bigger hit than Liberia, which serves the popular beaches and resorts of Costa Rica's Guanacaste region.

Advance bookings to San José for December and January are lagging behind last year, according to Cirium. Liberia is also seeing a decline.

Cirium cautioned that the booking figures do not include all reservations made directly with airlines.

The changes follow several airline service reductions this year. 

JetBlue suspended service from Orlando, while Frontier paused its San José flights between August and October, according to an October report from Costa Rica's Center for Tourism Studies (CET).

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The decline has been more pronounced in San José. 

In October, the airport there had 70 fewer weekly flights than a year earlier, while Liberia gained 10, the report found.

For Americans eyeing a Costa Rica getaway, the decline in service comes as ticket prices are also climbing.

Cirium data shows airfares from the U.S. were higher throughout the first eight months of 2026 than during the same period in 2025.

By August, the average fare had reached about $391, compared with roughly $276 a year earlier.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The reduction in flights is particularly significant for Costa Rica, where the U.S. accounts for nearly half of the country's scheduled airline seats, according to CET. 

Tourism is also a major source of revenue for the country, generating about $5.54 billion in 2025, according to data from the Costa Rican Tourism Institute.

While fewer seats do not necessarily mean fewer tourists will ultimately visit, the changes could leave some American travelers with fewer nonstop flights to choose from as they plan winter trips.

Guanacaste has also drawn attention from U.S. travelers for a separate health concern this year.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued a Level 2 Travel Health Notice for the province in July amid a chikungunya outbreak, Fox News Digital previously reported, with most reported cases centered around the popular beach destination of Playa Langosta.

The CDC advised travelers visiting the area to take extra precautions against mosquito bites, including using insect repellent and wearing long-sleeved shirts and pants.

item.title: Carville dares far-left to 'run somebody' against mainstream Dems in primary and end their 'civil war'
item.description: James Carville challenged the far-left wing of the Democratic Party to test its popularity and run a dream candidate against mainstream rivals in the 2028 presidential primary.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville challenged far-left Democrats to pick a candidate to represent them and see how well that candidate performs against mainstream Democrats in the 2028 presidential primary.

Carville argued on his "Politics War Room" podcast that, after briefly uniting to win a coalition victory against President Donald Trump, the Democratic Party is now due for a "civil war" among its ranks. However, he suggested the far left had overestimated its popularity. 

Carville challenged the progressives in his party to run their ideal candidate in the Democratic primary and let voters decide.

"The opinion that should matter, the most important opinion in all of this are people that vote in Democratic primaries for president of the United States," he said.

JAMES CARVILLE PREDICTS A 2028 'RECKONING' AS SOCIALIST CANDIDATES EYE THE DEMOCRATIC TICKET

"Stop running your mouth and run somebody," Carville said. "This is my proposal. You rally around a candidate that embodies the message and the values of ‘true progressivism.’ This is ‘Medicare-for-all.’ This is ‘question the very fundamental value of capitalism.’ 'We're not for incremental change. We're for change.’ Run somebody."

Carville said the candidate would be welcome at any debate and, if anything, would likely be favored by the media over mainstream candidates.

"I got news for you. The f---ing press will be pulling for you. OK?" he said.

"So, you're going to have a lot of advantages going in," Carville continued. "You're going to have a very sympathetic press. You're going to have a singular person that you and all of your friends and people that think like you, can all rally around.

"And then let's accept the verdict of the voters that vote in Democratic primaries for president of the United States."

JAMES CARVILLE WARNS FAR-LEFT CANDIDATES 'TOO HARD-HEADED' TO KNOW THEY'RE UNPOPULAR

Carville argued that the primary would test whether "your message is so popular that there are tens of millions or hundreds of millions of people that are dormant and waiting to be activated at the sound of the true bugle of progressivism, and they'll rise up in untold numbers."

However, he warned that every candidate should be asked on stage if they would support the eventual Democratic presidential nominee. If progressive candidates refuse to do so, he challenged them to reveal this upfront.

"But g--damn it, let's trust the Democratic primary voter," he suggested. "Yeah, that's a unique idea that maybe voters have a say so in this."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Democratic strategist Julian Epstein told Fox News Digital he disagreed with Carville's argument.

"There is a complete contradiction in this soliloquy," he said. "On the one hand, he is saying the elites should pick a progressive candidate. In the next breath, he says the voters should choose. The bigger issue is that this eludes the more fundamental challenge facing the Democrats.

"Democrats still have a toxic brand with about 28% of voters approving it and about 7-in-10 voters thinking the party's out of touch," Epstein said. "The party is far to the left of the median voter. The presidential primary process, with the activists and the NGO industrial complex, will pull the party further to the left.

"The answer is finding a modern-day equivalent of a Bill Clinton who has the personal charisma and the policy ingenuity to say no to the radical left and to meet the voters where they are," he continued. "We have been, and continue to be, a center-right country.

"The socialist movement may be in touch with the rage culture of influencer social media, but they are out of touch with the average voter," Epstein added. 

"This is the paradox the Democratic Party has to figure out. Progressive elites selecting a candidate before the primary is totally besides the point."

item.title: New statements from Rob Manfred, MLBPA, guarantee baseball is shut down indefinitely in two weeks | Ian Miller
item.description: MLB commissioner Rob Manfred says owners will not compromise on a salary cap and floor as CBA negotiations with the MLBPA near a Dec. 2 lockout.
item.content:encoded:
The day that fans of professional baseball have been dreading is rapidly approaching.

As we sit on Wednesday afternoon, we're just two weeks removed from the expiration of the Collective Bargaining Agreement between the 30 Major League Baseball owners and the MLB Players Association. The last round of CBA negotiations between the two sides started in December 2021 and stretched for nearly 100 days, pushing back the start of the 2022 regular season and requiring several adjustments to the 162-game schedule.

That negotiation was fairly straightforward. There were disagreements between the two sides, as there always is, but seeming agreement about the broad structure of baseball and keeping it in place.

BRYCE HARPER IMPLIES THERE WON'T BE A 2027 MLB SEASON, ADMITS HE ENJOYS OFFSEASON MORE THAN PLAYING

This time? Not so much.

The 30 owners have put their foot down, at least, through public statements, about their commitment to completely reshaping how baseball works. As has been widely reported, this means the introduction of a salary cap and associated floor.

YANKEES OWNER HAL STEINBRENNER CONFIRMS HE SUPPORTS OWNERS' SALARY CAP PROPOSALS AHEAD OF LIKELY MLB LOCKOUT

While most other domestic professional sports leagues have a salary cap, baseball is a holdout in avoiding this form of sports socialism. MLB's current format already includes revenue sharing, where higher-income teams redistribute their revenue to smaller market teams, and any number of artificial controls on player movement in the early part of their career.

Generally, players are prohibited from reaching the open market for six seasons after their Major League debut. Given that most players reach their physical peak at around 26–27, often, reaching free agency at around 30 means the team that drafted, or signed, and then developed that player already had control of the ascendant stage of their career.

Even that, though, isn't enough. Because owners are committed to increasing their profits and franchise valuations first and foremost, and because many fans have been misled into thinking that theLos Angeles Dodgers are some sort of baseball-ruining enemy, commissioner Rob Manfred has been adamant that the owners will push for a salary cap.

The players, meanwhile, have been adamant that they will reject any attempt at a cap. And so here we find ourselves, two weeks away from D-Day, with no end in sight.

MLB OWNERS ARE BACK WITH A NEW SALARY CAP PROPOSAL TO SHUT DOWN SPORT EVEN AFTER BREWERS WIN WORLD SERIES

In fact, on Wednesday, Manfred made some ominous comments about ownership's resolve at limiting player compensation.

"I will say there's plenty of room for compromise," he said Wednesday at a news conference around the owners' meetings. "But there's one thing I will not compromise, and that's the issue that we're hearing from the vast majority of our fans: They want salary cap and floor, and on that, we will not compromise."

Manfred, being apparently unaware of how words work, then said that the MLB Players Association needs to compromise with them.

"We made the proposal way back in May," he added. "Another word for 'nonstarter' over months is a refusal to bargain. I think it's time that the MLBPA needs to realize that this proposal is serious. I'm not suggesting they need to accept it wholecloth. I think they need to look at the proposal and try to find some ways to move to the middle as opposed to making no proposal at all."

In response, MLBPA head Bruce Meyer issued a statement criticizing Manfred and ownership's stance.

"There can be no clearer example of the league's lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts," the statement said.

"There should be no illusions about the owners' true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Manfred did say that a lockout may not be an inevitability, that he would be ready and willing to work through Thanksgiving to get a deal done.

"A decision on a lockout is one that we're going to make at the last possible moment," he said. "We're going to devote ourselves to the bargaining process. I'm not that big on Thanksgiving as a holiday. We'll make ourselves available whenever and wherever to bargain in an effort to make an agreement."

So the league's stance effectively boils down to, we won't compromise on the single biggest issue that we're negotiating over, but the players need to compromise and give up their biggest advantage to make us richer, and we'll negotiate quickly as long as players agree with what we want. Perfect!

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Make no mistake, regardless of Manfred's comments, this is heading towards a lockout. Owners are going to lock players out of team facilities, by choice, on December 2. Because they want to, not because they have to. And fans do share some of the blame.

For whatever reason, the Dodgers' success in 2024 and 2025 has shortened fan memories, to the point where they apparently forgot that decades ago, it became apparent that there is no formula for winning in the postseason. There is no way to buy a championship, because baseball is too unpredictable. The league's claims, which were inexplicably lapped up, that small market teams have no "hope" of winning, were proven comprehensively false by the Milwaukee Brewers winning the 2026 World Series in one of the dominant playoff runs in the history of the sport.

Oh, and the team they beat, the Tampa Bay Rays, swept the New York Yankees to get there.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

This wasn't an aberration or outlier; the Rays have reached the World Series twice in the last seven seasons, more than the Yankees, Mets, Red Sox, Giants and Cubs combined over that time frame. Milwaukee has the best winning percentage in baseball from 2025-2026. Cleveland has been one of the most consistent postseason teams in MLB. The Toronto Blue Jays, for all their spending, have not won a World Series. The Philadelphia Phillies, again, with all their spending, have reached the World Series one time over the last 17 seasons and have zero championships in that time frame.

Competitive balance in baseball is better than most other major sports, because of its inherent randomness. Fans, though, bought the league's arguments, and the league is now taking advantage of it by shutting the sport down two weeks from today.

So how long will this last? Is the 2027 season really in jeopardy?

The answer is nobody knows, and yes. The last lockout lasted 99 days, but again, did not involve the level of fundamental disagreement that this negotiation does. Hopefully Manfred's comments are another negotiating tactic meant to show ownership's resolve, but if they really are serious about a salary cap, it could mean a lengthy work stoppage that drags into the 2027 season.

Players, understandably, do not want to give up the opportunity to earn as much as the market will pay them. Just like any employee with competing job offers wants to negotiate the most they can get in salary. Owners, who do not care one bit about competitive balance, want to take advantage of this current moment to make even more money.

Instead of a "50/50" revenue split, they'd take billions of associated baseball revenue off the top first. For example, saying you'll share a six-pack of drinks and then taking two out of the package for yourself, and splitting the final four. Why? Because it limits their exposure, increases franchise valuations to compete with the NFL, and generates more profits.

That's the prerogative. But if they choose to stick to it, they might lose a lot more fans by missing games than they'd lose from not imposing new limitations on player salaries. Two weeks out, there have been little signs of progress, and many signs that the two sides appear just as far apart as they always have.

Not a great sign for baseball.

item.title: Multiple Bigfoot sightings reported by gamers who have gotten their hands on 'GTA VI'
item.description: Players report "GTA VI" Bigfoot sightings in the woods of Leonida, with video showing gamers knocked out by noxious fumes before enormous feet approach.
item.content:encoded:

As "Grand Theft Auto VI" rolls out worldwide on November 19, 2026, and receives high marks, gamers are documenting different aspects of the game. You can go jet-skiing with a dog. You can get busted for stealing an old lady's scooter.

There are even encounters with wildlife that don't always work out in your character's favor. I've seen tiger attacks and people get eaten by an alligator.

That takes me to the rabbit hole I went down this afternoon on Twitter. The Bigfoot encounters, of which there are many, appear to be taking place in and around the woods of Leonida, reports Game Spot.

Some players have ended up being knocked out in the woods by a noxious fumes-emitting effigy. As they drift into unconsciousness, Bigfoot's enormous feet can be seen approaching them.

Bigfoot has been everywhere these days. It only stands to reason that the folklore legend would show up in one of the most highly anticipated games ever.

REDDIT'S BIRDING COMMUNITY GOES WILD AS UNIQUE 'GRAND THEFT AUTO 6' FEATURE COMES TO LIGHT

I haven’t purchased the game, therefore I won't be in the reported group of about 1 in 5 salaried employees who are taking time off from work to play "GTA VI" as soon as it comes out.

Prior to the Bigfoot sightings, I admit that I was planning on purchasing "Grand Theft Auto VI" at some point.

Now that you can, among everything else, spend some time in the woods getting abducted by Bigfoot or whatever happens after you've been knocked out by the smell, that purchase might have to come a little sooner.

As much fun as running around shirtless creating chaos at airports sounds (seemingly part of the game), finding actual evidence of Bigfoot is much more intriguing to me.

item.title: Irish activist indicted in US over alleged destruction of $60M military plane
item.description: United States prosecutors say Daithi O'Corrain spent months planning the Shannon Airport attack that left a $60 million C-130H Hercules beyond repair
item.content:encoded:
An Irish anti-Israel activist was indicted in the United States after allegedly destroying a $60 million American military aircraft at an airport in Ireland, leaving the plane damaged beyond repair after what prosecutors described as months of meticulous planning.

Federal prosecutors announced the indictment Tuesday, seven months after Daithi O'Corrain, 48, allegedly breached the security perimeter at Shannon Airport in western Ireland and broke into an unoccupied U.S. Air National Guard C-130H Hercules aircraft.

Prosecutors said O'Corrain then spent hours damaging the aircraft, cutting critical wiring and hydraulic lines, smashing cockpit instruments, puncturing air ducts and pinching shut the aircraft's liquid oxygen line.

2 FOREIGN NATIONALS BREACH UK BASE HOUSING KEY US, NATO INTEL HUB AMID $556M EXPANSION

The damage was so extensive it rendered the aircraft inoperable, and the $60 million plane will never return to active flight status, according to federal authorities.

Photographs released by federal prosecutors show extensive damage inside the aircraft, including smashed cockpit instruments, severed wiring and damaged equipment. Other images show tools allegedly used in the attack and O'Corrain standing on the aircraft's roof before his arrest.

According to the indictment, O'Corrain spent months researching the aircraft's construction, acquiring tools and gallium, a metal capable of corroding aluminum, and using a flight-tracking app to monitor military aircraft. He also researched previous attacks on U.S. military planes at Shannon Airport and searched for locations where he could breach the airport's security perimeter.

O'Corrain, who also goes by the name David Curran and is from County Cork in southern Ireland, was charged with destruction of government property, which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison.

FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle Jr. said the attack was meticulously planned and jeopardized critical military operations.

"This was not an act of spontaneous vandalism. The defendant allegedly spent months researching the aircraft, acquiring tools and materials and preparing to maximize the destruction he could inflict," Barnacle said. 

"The FBI and our law enforcement partners will continue to pursue anyone who targets U.S. military assets, regardless of where those attacks occur."

US EVACUATES 13 MILITARY AIRCRAFT FROM SECOND UK BASE AS NEW IRAN THREAT RAISES ALARM

It remains unclear whether the United States has formally requested O'Corrain's extradition from Ireland. The Justice Department, Irish Department of Justice and Irish prosecutors did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment before publication.

The C-130 Hercules is a four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft used to carry troops, equipment and supplies, including into remote areas with short, rough runways. First introduced in the 1950s, it remains in service today, while the C-130H variant involved in the Shannon Airport incident dates to the 1970s. The aircraft was parked on a taxiway and was due to depart for another country on a U.S. military assignment, according to the indictment.

The indictment outlined how the alleged attack unfolded.

O'Corrain allegedly breached Shannon Airport's security perimeter at approximately 4:40 a.m. on April 11 before crossing the airfield and breaking through the aircraft's rear crew door. Once inside, he barricaded himself using tools and supplies he had brought with him. He also covered the aircraft's windows with the flight crew's hammocks, except for the cockpit windows, prosecutors said.

Prosecutors said he demonstrated detailed knowledge of the aircraft's critical components and how to destroy them while protecting himself. They warned that the aircraft could have been rocked by a massive explosion had O'Corrain cut through its liquid oxygen line instead of pinching it shut.

Five hours later, the flight crew returned to prepare for departure and spotted O'Corrain through a cockpit window, prompting them to alert airport security.

O'Corrain allegedly climbed through a roof hatch and continued damaging the aircraft, striking its exterior with an axe and pouring unidentified substances and placing objects, including ball bearings, into its fuel tanks. Video circulating online at the time appeared to show a man in dark clothing walking along the wing of the aircraft near the engines and fuselage.

Irish police arrived shortly afterward and arrested him.

"These charges send a clear and powerful message that attacks on U.S. military assets — and thus our national security — will not be tolerated," U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald said.

O'Corrain is also facing criminal charges in Ireland over the same incident. He was initially denied bail before securing his release through the Irish High Court, according to RTÉ.

Irish prosecutors have since moved to bring the case to trial, with O'Corrain facing charges, including criminal damage to the aircraft and interference with airport operations. He is scheduled to appear in court again in January.

O'Corrain has drawn support from pro-Palestinian activists in Ireland.

An online fundraiser describes him as an independent peace activist and portrays the incident as an act of resistance against the U.S. military's presence in Ireland and American support for Israel. The campaign features a raised fist gripping a hammer — imagery associated with labor and revolutionary movements — superimposed over a photograph of the aircraft.

"An inspiring act of direct action was carried out at Shannon Airport to resist the unwanted presence of the US Military in Ireland in the face of their illegal war & support of Israel’s genocide," organizer Tracey Ryan wrote.

Shannon Airport, which has long served as a transit hub for U.S. military aircraft, was also used by President Donald Trump and Air Force One during his visit to Ireland in September.

The alleged attack followed three other security breaches at Shannon Airport in 2025, according to the indictment. In May, three people were arrested after driving a van through the airport's perimeter fence. Weeks later, three others breached the airfield and sprayed a U.S. military aircraft with paint, temporarily grounding it.

In November 2025, three more people drove a van through the airport's security perimeter and entered a restricted area near a U.S. military C-40 aircraft before being intercepted by security personnel.

Unlike those earlier incidents, the April attack allegedly resulted in the permanent loss of a U.S. military aircraft, with O'Corrain now facing prosecution in two countries.

item.title: Two bad teams, one cheap ticket: Jets-Chargers seats barely cost more than a SoFi cheeseburger
item.description: Aaron Glenn's New York Jets have lost five straight, and the matchup with the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers has fans paying just $26 as both teams eye the NFL Draft instead.
item.content:encoded:
When you look at the Week 11 slate, there is one game your eyes stop at.

You tell your friends and family not to bother you for a few hours during the 4 p.m. slate on Sunday because this matchup is a can’t-miss. The stadium will be rocking, and the ticket prices are exorbitant.

The matchup between the Los Angeles Chargers and the New York Jets is appointment viewing. Not. The Chargers are 1-8 and the Jets are 2-8.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

This game is actually the definition of a can-miss game. Chargers-Jets means more for NFL Draft implications than anything else, and the ticket prices reflect that.

If you are bored in the greater Los Angeles area on Sunday afternoon, you can get into the stadium for a grand total of $26 to watch Justin Herbert and Geno Smith sling the rock at SoFi Stadium.

A burger in SoFi Stadium is $14, which is almost as expensive as the ticket itself!

For the first time all season, the Chargers are coming off a win. They upset the Jacoby Brissett-led Baltimore Ravens on Monday, winning 23-20.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Unfortunately for the Chargers, the ticket prices didn’t exactly shoot up following the win as fans' excitement for the season faded away months ago. The Chargers came into the season touted as an AFC contender, as the addition of former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator had people thinking Los Angeles was ready to take the next step.

Instead, their offense has gone in reverse. The Chargers have scored just 16 points per game, which is last in the NFL.

As for the Jets, there was hope at the beginning of the season. The offense looked revamped with Geno Smith at quarterback and head coach Aaron Glenn taking over defensive play-calling, but the wheels quickly fell off the cart.

The Jets have lost five games in a row, and Glenn arguably has the hottest seat in the NFL in just his second year as head coach.

The moribund Jets will likely be starting over with another head coach next season, along with a quarterback they can select at the top of April’s NFL Draft.

The combination of the Chargers being the NFL’s disappointing team and the Jets, well, being the same old Jets, has led to the cheap tickets.

item.title: Giants' Cam Skattebo putting his backflip on the back burner after seeing Aidan Hutchinson celebration injury
item.description: Cam Skattebo says his New York Giants backflip celebration is done after Aidan Hutchinson's knee injury, though a playoff moment could bring it back.
item.content:encoded:
Cam Skattebo's signature touchdown celebration is officially on the shelf.

The New York Giants running back, who is much better known for his backflips after scoring than just about anything else he does on the football field, has apparently decided that celly can be catastrophic.

So Skattebo doesn't see himself repeating the move any longer after watching Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson blow out his right knee during a sack celebration of Drake Maye last Sunday in Germany.

LIONS' STAR HURT CELEBRATING SACK OF PATRIOTS’ DRAKE MAYE AS BOTH INJURED ON POSSIBLY SEASON-ALTERING PLAY

"It's hard to see," Skattebo told a couple of reporters on Wednesday, according to the New York Post. "I'm saying, yeah [no more]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.'

"That ain't going to happen to me."

This retirement of the backflip comes with caveats:

If he simply forgets and instincts take over, it might happen. And big moments like a Super Bowl win or something otherwise notable might bring back the flip.

"If we go to the playoffs or something," Skattebo said.

Skattebo, it should be noted, is in only his second season with the Giants and has struggled with his share of injuries.

GIANTS' CAM SKATTEBO VOWS TO MAINTAIN VIOLENT PLAYING STYLE AFTER GRUESOME ANKLE INJURY

During Week 8 of the 2025 season against the Philadelphia Eagles, Skattebo suffered a gruesome right ankle injury. The trauma resulted in a dislocated ankle, a fractured fibula, and a ruptured deltoid ligament.

In October, Skattebo suffered a Grade 1 hamstring strain and missed one game as a result.

CAM SKATTEBO HORRIFIES GIANTS FANS BY ATTEMPTING A BACKFLIP DESPITE COMING OFF A LEG INJURY

Despite the injuries, Skattebo previously defended continuing his backflips.

Following a viral incident where he botched a backflip on a bouncy WWE/Fanatics Fest floor — raising concerns because it came on the heels of last year's major injury — Skattebo brushed off suggestions he stop.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

He noted that he had been doing backflips since he was four years old and stated, "I will not hurt myself before the season."

In the 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders on Nov. 12, Skattebo scored two touchdowns and after one of those he was actually joined by other teammates doing backflips.

It's unclear if group flipping is also going away.

item.title: Pat McAfee and crew roast ESPN's Heather Dinich for absurd College Football Playoff metrics
item.description: Pat McAfee's crew ripped ESPN's Heather Dinich over her "Strength of Conference" metric as College Football Playoff rankings spark SEC bias chatter.
item.content:encoded:
A lot has been made about the latest College Football Playoff rankings, though when is that ever not the case?

I'm not here to discuss whether or not the powers that be are in cahoots with any one conference or if ESPN is exhibiting "SEC bias," but there seems to be a lot of chatter on social media, almost too much to ignore.

Most of this stems from The Worldwide Leader's wrap-up coverage from Tuesday night's CFP rankings reveal, during which ESPN's Heather Dinich unveiled a new metric called "Strength of Conference."

ESPN'S HEATHER DINICH DESTROYED BY CFB FANS OVER MYSTERY PLAYOFF RANKING METRIC, UCLA CHEERLEADERS & TARPS OFF

Dinich took plenty of heat for this, most of which came from fans online, but one prominent voice that works for the very same network may have just fired off a shot inside the ESPN tent.

Pat McAfee had Reece Davis on to make sense of what many are calling the most confusing CFP rankings in the history of the sport, and after Davis exited stage right, the boys took their own employer to task.

"It is hard not to just be like, 'there's a lot of SEC representation in there,'" McAfee said.

He also pointed out that there are plenty of SEC athletic directors who are on the CFP selection committee, and that Mark Dantonio might need to start "swinging a bit bigger fist."

NEW COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF POLL PROVES THE SELECTION COMMITTEE IS JUST MAKING IT UP AS THEY GO

That's when Ty Schmitt, one of McAfee's crew members, dropped the bomb, referring to Dinich as a "turncoat."

McAfee let out a sarcastic "no," before a voice off camera accused her of "making up new metrics."

"She couldn't explain it worth a damn," Schmitt said.

Obviously, the ribbing is mostly tongue-in-cheek from McAfee and crew, and if Dinich were on set with them, they’d be dishing it out right to her face.

I don't think there's anything nefarious going on here, but it is funny to see even people within the ESPN umbrella pushing the narrative that the CFP committee is compromised.

I wonder if Pat will be receiving a call from some of the higher-ups telling him to tone it down?

I digress.

Again, I'm not here to make a stink of the CFP rankings. I'll leave that to guys like Ian Miller (also, my Florida Gators are part of the problem as a ranked four-loss team, so I must recuse myself).

Suffice to say, we have a few weeks left until these rankings are actually final, so if I were you all, I'd save my breath until things are written in stone.

But then again, where's the fun in that?

item.title: Glen Powell’s ‘Comeback King’ trailer packs country star power, but divides fans
item.description: Glen Powell trained in singing and guitar and co-wrote the screenplay with Judd Apatow for "The Comeback King," playing a country star in free-fall.
item.content:encoded:
Glen Powell is cracking beers and throwing on cowboy boots in his upcoming comedy, "The Comeback King."

The first trailer, which debuted Nov. 18, offered fans a glimpse of Powell as Aubrey King, a country music superstar whose career comes crashing down after a public breakup with his pop star girlfriend Missy, played by "Outer Banks" star Madelyn Cline.

King discovers Missy is cheating on him, but she goes on to make a breakup anthem that makes it seem like he was unfaithful.

The comedy features appearances from some of country music's biggest names, including Reba McEntire, Miranda Lambert, Jelly Roll, Brad Paisley, Chris Stapleton, Luke Bryan and Shaboozey. In one memorable trailer moment, McEntire's character confronts Powell after he accidentally punches her during an altercation.

GLEN POWELL REVEALS WILD NIGHT WITH COUNTRY STARS ENDED WITH BEER PONG AT JELLY ROLL’S NASHVILLE BAR

McEntire responds by tackling King to the ground and pulling out a pocket knife.

"I’m Reba frickin’ McEntire," the Queen of Country says. "How do you wanna die?"

The trailer quickly generated conversation online, with viewers offering a range of reactions to Powell's latest big-screen venture. While some fans were immediately sold on the actor's country music transformation and the movie's impressive lineup of celebrity cameos, others questioned whether the comedy would deliver on its premise.

"First movie I've wanted to see in a long time," one user wrote on X.

"Glen Powell, Madelyn Cline, Megan Moroney and lots of other country artists," another added. "I'm so sat."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"Glen Powell in a comedy like this? I'm already interested," one said. "This looks like it could be a fun watch. Can't wait to see how it turns out."

"Glen Powell playing a country star in free-fall is the most believable comeback pitch of 2027," another wrote.

But the excitement wasn't universal. Some social media users were quick to criticize the trailer, questioning whether the star-studded comedy would actually deliver laughs.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Is it just me or does this not look particularly funny," one user commented on X. "Seems more like a drama with a few funny lines. Judd Apatow has lost his ability to be funny."

"I thought Glen Powell was our next Tom Cruise," a user said. "Only Steven Seagal can save us now."

"This looks atrocious," another added.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Powell rose to mainstream fame playing Lt. Jake "Hangman" Seresin opposite Cruise in "Top Gun: Maverick." His other notable projects include "Hidden Figures," "Anyone But You," "Hit Man" and "Twisters."

Beyond starring in "The Comeback King," Powell co-wrote the screenplay with Apatow and trained in singing and guitar to portray the fictional country singer. The movie marks another major step in Powell's expanding Hollywood career, combining his comedic talents with an unexpected musical turn.

The movie is set to hit theaters Feb. 5, 2027.

item.title: Japan scrambles fighter jets after Russian aircraft breach airspace amid rising Pacific tensions
item.description: Suspected Russian aircraft entered Japanese airspace near Okinoshima, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi warned of instability at the Quad Leaders Summit.
item.content:encoded:
Japan scrambled fighter jets early Tuesday after two suspected Russian aircraft entered Japanese airspace, prompting a rapid military response ahead of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's warning of rising global instability during the Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila.

Hours later, President Donald Trump had also joined Takaichi, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the summit, where the leaders voiced opposition to actions threatening regional peace and stability.

"We strongly oppose any destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability," the leaders said in a joint statement later released by the White House.

TRUMP KICKS OFF HIGH-STAKES ASIA TRIP WITH XI, PUTIN MEETINGS LOOMING ON WORLD STAGE

On Wednesday, two U.S. military officials confirmed to Fox News that the aircraft carrier USS George Washington was departing the Middle East for the Pacific.

Sen. Mazie Hirono, D-Hawaii, questioned acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao Tuesday about the lack of aircraft carriers in the Pacific, noting that three carrier strike groups had been deployed to the Middle East.

"There are none in the Indo-Pacific area when we are looking at China, not to mention North Korea and especially what China may have in mind," Hirono said.

"See, this is stretching and stressing our resources. You can't take away the strike group out of the Indo-Pacific."

The Russian aircraft entered Japanese airspace northwest of Okinoshima, an island in southwestern Japan's Fukuoka Prefecture, at about 4:07 a.m. local time Nov. 17, according to Japan's Defense Ministry.

Fighter jets from the Japan Air Self-Defense Force's Western Air Defense Force were scrambled to issue warnings and take other measures, the ministry said in a statement posted on X.

The first suspected Russian aircraft entered Japanese airspace at approximately 4:07 a.m. and remained for three minutes. 

A second aircraft entered the same area at approximately 4:09 a.m. and departed three minutes later.

THREE MANILA MOMENTS THAT GIVE TRUMP MOMENTUM GOING INTO TALKS WITH CHINA

Japan's Defense Ministry said the aircraft traveled through the Tsushima Strait and passed between Japan's Yonaguni Island and Taiwan before continuing into the Pacific Ocean.

"In response, the Self-Defense Forces scrambled fighter jets from the Japan Air Self-Defense Force’s Western Air Defense Force to issue notifications and warnings and take other measures," the Ministry of Defense said.

Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said Tokyo lodged a strong protest with Moscow and demanded measures to prevent further airspace violations.

The incidents "not only constitute a grave infringement upon Japan’s sovereignty but also pose a threat to our security. They are entirely unacceptable," Koizumi said.

This came as Takaichi warned of growing instability in the international order and promised a bigger role for Japan in maintaining regional security.

CHINA, RUSSIA, IRAN AND NORTH KOREA FORM 'AXIS OF AGGRESSORS' THAT COULD OVERWHELM US, BOOK WARNS

"While the international order is experiencing a period of great instability, Japan will play a more proactive role," Takaichi said during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in Manila.

Takaichi emphasized Japan's commitment to maintaining an international order based on freedom, openness and the rule of law while strengthening cooperation with Southeast Asian nations.

"Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable and prosperous Indo-Pacific," Trump had also said ahead of the Quad meeting.

The leaders had expressed "grave concerns" about economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions, and outlined plans for a joint military exercise involving maritime patrol aircraft in 2027.

KIM JONG UN'S NUCLEAR BUILDUP SPARKS 'SERIOUS CONCERN' AHEAD OF TRUMP-XI-PUTIN SUMMIT

The airspace incursion comes amid broader security concerns across the Indo-Pacific, where Japan and its regional partners have increasingly monitored Russian and Chinese military activity.

On Tuesday, South Korea’s air force also scrambled fighter jets as multiple Russian military aircraft had entered the country’s air defense identification zone, according to the Ministry of National Defense.

Otherwise, Japan's relations with Moscow have deteriorated since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, with Tokyo joining Western allies in imposing sanctions on the Kremlin.

The two countries are also locked in a decades-old territorial dispute over islands north of Japan's northernmost main island of Hokkaido. Russia administers the islands, which Japan claims as its Northern Territories.

Japan previously scrambled fighter jets in 2024 after a Russian military patrol aircraft entered Japanese airspace near Hokkaido three times.

item.title: Dozens of Army soldiers sign up for unique reenlistment incentive to play Grand Theft Auto VI
item.description: The U.S. Army offered Fort Stewart soldiers four-day passes to play "Grand Theft Auto VI" as a reenlistment perk, and 43 of 130 eligible troops took it.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Army turned to one of the year’s most anticipated video games to get soldiers at Fort Stewart, Georgia, talking about reenlisting.

The offer was a four-day pass to play "Grand Theft Auto VI" when it launches Thursday.

The Army said 43 of the 130 eligible soldiers in the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion chose the perk when they reenlisted for two to six more years, Task & Purpose first reported.

NBA PLAYER PREDICTS AMERICAN ATHLETES' PERFORMANCES WILL DIP IN NOVEMBER WHILE THEY PLAY GTA

"I’m all campaign. I’m all about the heist," Sgt. Jamire Smith, a combat engineer who signed up for six more years in the Army and took the four-day pass, told Task & Purpose. "I think I have a good 24 hours to waste on it."

Smith said he had been close to leaving the Army before leaders in his company and battalion showed him they still needed his skills. He qualified for a roughly $60,000 reenlistment bonus after training to drive heavy breaching vehicles, the outlet reported.

US ARMY HITS 2026 RECRUITING GOALS FOUR MONTHS EARLY, PETE HEGSETH ANNOUNCES AT WEST POINT COMMENCEMENT

The battalion offered the pass from Aug. 1 through Nov. 14. The Army said the time off came on top of standard reenlistment incentives, which can include cash bonuses or a choice of duty station depending on a soldier’s eligibility and the Army’s needs.

Staff Sgt. Brittany Wolfer, the battalion’s career counselor, called the perk an "eye grabber." She pitched it to her commander after hearing Sgt. Maj. Celeste R. Spencer, a senior Army career counselor, float the idea on TikTok.

Wolfer said the battalion had gone about eight months without a career counselor before she arrived, and she wanted soldiers nearing a decision about reenlisting to know whom to talk to about their options.

The commander had played "Grand Theft Auto 2" and backed the idea, Wolfer told the outlet. Wolfer, a gamer herself, went to basic training the same week "Grand Theft Auto V" came out.

Staff Sgt. Floyd Maxwell, a network systems and communications specialist, signed up for three more years. He told the outlet his father, who died a few months ago, had encouraged him to make a career of the Army. He said the battalion had also given him a sense of family.

"The excitement from this incentive has sparked positive conversations amongst Soldiers to discuss the continuation of their service in the Army," the Army said in a statement. The service said it recognized the 3rd Infantry Division as its top division for retention in 2025.

MIAMI HEAT FINALLY UNVEIL 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED JERSEYS AND SOCIAL MEDIA IS LOVING THEM

The game has an Army connection of its own. One of its main characters, Jason Duval, served in the Army before going to work for drug runners in the Florida Keys, according to Rockstar Games. Wolfer had a suggestion for the studio, too. She wants it to put Rocky the Bulldog, the 3rd Infantry Division’s mascot, in the game.

"Grand Theft Auto VI" had already brought in an estimated $1.65 billion from more than 17 million preorders by Wednesday, Forbes reported, citing market research firm Sensor Tower.

MIAMI HEAT UNVEIL VICE CITY COURT FOR 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED CLASH WITH MILWAUKEE BUCKS

Hours before the U.S. launch, PlayStation warned that a network disruption could make it difficult for some players to launch games or access online features.

Its status page showed the issue was resolved by 2:30 p.m. ET, Axios reported. Rockstar says the game unlocks at midnight local time Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Army for comment.

Fox News' Liz Friden contributed to this report.

item.title: What is Baltimore best at making? 'Criminals,' says Marlon Humphrey who then feels the heat and changes tune
item.description: Marlon Humphrey says Baltimore is best at making "criminals" on his podcast, then apologizes as backlash erupts on social media over the crime jab.
item.content:encoded:
Marlon Humphrey is sorry. No, really. He took a jab at the city of Baltimore and its crime rate this week and had to quickly walk that back with an apology on Wednesday.

The Baltimore Ravens defensive back in his latest Marlon Humphrey podcast took on the question of what Baltimore is best at making?

So ... crab cakes?

Old Bay Seasoning?

Baltimore’s crime rates are historically higher than the national average and rank it among the higher-crime large metropolitan areas in the United States.

Analyses from various public safety trackers consistently place Baltimore among the leaders per capita for both violent and property crime, outpacing the vast majority of U.S. cities.

Baltimore residents spent the past few hours rallying to the side of their town and it started on social media.

item.title: Flu activity rises across US as 6 states reach high levels, CDC data shows
item.description: Cases of the flu are spiking early nationwide, with the CDC reporting Louisiana at very high activity and influenza A (H1N1) the top virus this season.
item.content:encoded:
Cases of the flu are already cropping up across the country in an early spike.

In its weekly influenza update, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has alerted that seasonal flu activity is "higher than typically observed at this time of year."

About 11% of specimens tested for flu at clinical labs were positive in the week ending Nov. 7, with that percentage rising. The CDC also reported more than 3% of doctors’ office visits were due to flu-like symptoms.
