New York, Massachusetts and Hawaii were in the CDC map’s moderate category for influenza-like illness in the week ending Nov. 7 (week 44).

California, Tennessee and Oregon were in the high category for influenza-like illness, along with South Carolina and Texas. Louisiana was the only state in the very high category, according to the CDC’s Week 44 map.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The CDC noted that an earlier increase in activity does not predict a higher seasonal peak or overall severity.

While it’s too early to know which flu viruses will be most dominant this season, in the week ending Nov. 7, the most frequently reported virus was influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, a descendant of the strain that caused the 2009 swine flu pandemic and has circulated seasonally since.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The CDC estimates that there have been 2.6 million illnesses, 36,000 hospitalizations and 2,100 deaths tied to flu infections so far this season. Five flu-associated deaths among children have been reported to the agency.

In an October media briefing, Dr. Anna Durbin of Johns Hopkins University stated that the flu hospitalization rate in mid-October was the highest it’s been in 15 years.

"Because the flu season is starting a bit earlier, I think it's really important for everyone to get a flu vaccine as soon as possible," she advised.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Dr. Fred Lopez, an infectious diseases specialist at the LSU Health Sciences Center in New Orleans, told the Associated Press that flu season is "taking off in a direction that’s only likely to increase in the next month or two."

"If you haven’t been vaccinated, you should get vaccinated now," he added.

The CDC recommends an annual flu vaccine for everyone 6 months and older. Prescription antiviral drugs can treat flu and should be started as early as possible, especially for people at higher risk of complications.

With Thanksgiving approaching, doctors expect flu and other respiratory viruses to spread as people travel and gather with friends and family.

Last winter, flu activity surged in late December. At the time, New York City health officials described the season as the city’s most intense in 20 years, according to the AP.

item.title: The next set of Winter Classic uniforms have arrived, and here are the 5 best the NHL has ever seen
item.description: The NHL's New Year's Day Winter Classic brings new Utah Mammoth and Colorado Avalanche jerseys to Salt Lake City, and one bold set is turning heads.
item.content:encoded:
It's a New Year's Day tradition like no other ... aside from the fact that sometimes it's on January 2. And this year it's on New Year's Eve.

Regardless, the point is this: the Winter Classic is one of the NHL's marquee events that usually gives us some of the best uniforms you'll ever see hitting the ice.

This year's game is at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City and pits the league's newest team, the Utah Mammoth, against the Colorado Avalanche.

It's a really solid divisional matchup that showcases the league's newest market and an iconic, picturesque stadium, but we're here to discuss the duds.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Lucky for us, they were released on Wednesday (before "Grand Theft Auto VI" takes over, which was probably a smart call).

Very good work from Fanatics on these.

Let's start with the Avs. They've got a crisp snow-white base, which is a welcome change of pace from the "vintage white" a lot of teams use in the Winter Classic. On top of it, they're going with an old-school striping pattern with a retro-styled crest, and — my favorite part — maroon buckets, gloves, and pants.

It's a sharp look, but it's a little safe.

Unlike the Mammoth, who are really going for it.

Utah is rolling out what looks to be a slightly different shade of blue (it could be the photo) with very old-school striping, a Mr. Snuffleupagus doppelgänger for a logo, and brown gloves and pants.

But not the light brown we normally see that is supposed to mimic old leather gear. It's a darker shade that matches Ol' Snuffy.

EVERYONE WANTS WHAT ONE MINOR LEAGUE BASEBALL TEAM PUT OUT AS A HILARIOUS TRIBUTE TO THE CAROLINA HURRICANES

It is an eye-catching set, and the Mammoth — who have really been crushing it with their jerseys, including their Hometown Remix sweaters — are going to sell a lot of these.

But what are the best Winter Classic jerseys of all time? Well, let's count them down.

The Stars will host the Vegas Golden Knights for a Stadium Series game later this season, but they had a really nice Winter Classic uniform when they faced the Nashville Predators (who had solid ones too) at the Cotton Bowl.

I'm a sucker for those retro-inspired brown gloves, but how did those sweaters not become a third jersey or even the basis for a rebrand?

They're so good, and there's a startling number of uniforms that didn't get enough time on the ice.

The Flyers' second Winter Classic appearance came in 2012, and since they haven't messed with their uniforms much in team history, they came up with a great faux back design.

The keystone patch for the captains was an awesome touch, and this one did see some time as a third jersey.

It was the best part of the game if you're a Flyers fan because the outcome ... well, it wasn't the most fun.

It's tough to top the OGs, and the Sabres and Penguins started the Winter Classic off on the right foot with a classic game and classic uniforms.

Both are great sets plucked from their respective histories, but the Penguins' powder blues really stand out.

Sidney Crosby winning the game in a shootout as it snowed at the old Ralph Wilson Stadium is one of the most iconic moments in Winter Classic history, and it sure doesn't hurt that they were wearing those beauties.

The second Winter Classic took place at Wrigley Field and saw the Blackhawks hosting the Detroit Red Wings.

The Blackhawks have been to quite a few Winter Classics, but this uniform is the runaway winner. The chest stripe with the logo in the roundel works so well.

Detroit had some cool getups which paid homage to the Detroit Cougars, but they couldn't top what the Hawks brought to the party ... even if it looked like Chicago raided the Portland Winterhawks' locker room.

Seeing as they were the league's newest team at the time, the Kraken dipped into Seattle hockey history and honored the Seattle Metropolitans — the first American team to win the Stanley Cup — with some all-time sweaters.

The barber pole can be a tough look to pull off, but the Kraken nailed it, and their recolored logo with the team name in it, like the one the Metropolitans used, is nothing short of outstanding.

It's the right mix of bold, historic, and just flat-out cool-looking that makes it the best Winter Classic uniform ever.

item.title: Mike Florio says Hitler joke about Mike Vrabel mustache is OK because it's been 80 years | Bobby Burack
item.description: Perennial OutKick Woke All-Star Mike Florio defended his Hitler joke about Mike Vrabel's mustache, saying it's been 80 years since the Holocaust.
item.content:encoded:
Perennial OutKick Woke All-Star Mike Florio says it's okay to make Hitler jokes because it's been 80 years since the Holocaust.

At least, that was his defense for joking about Patriots' head coach Mike Vrabel's mustache during the team's matchup against the Lions in Germany last week.

"He's got the German mustache," co-host Chris Simms said about Vrabel following a press conference.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"If you’re in Germany, you got to be careful trimming that thing," Florio joked back.

Their producer cringed at the joke, prompting Florio to respond, "It’s funny. … It was 80 years ago."

"Let us have some fun, for crying out loud," Florio added.

Listen below, via TMZ:

We are not the joke police. On the surface, we would not cover such a story. We all make jokes. Some land, some do not.

However, there's something rich about Mike Florio, one of the most professionally offended sportswriters in America, excusing Hitler jokes because he believes enough time has passed since the Holocaust.

This is the same Florio who fumed about President Trump's supposed "assault on DEI." He continues to pressure NFL teams to sign Colin Kaepernick, who has not played NFL football in a decade. He claimed Trump's immigration policy left him "shaken to [his] core." He claimed to be offended about Trump not posting about "Juneteenth."

Had anyone else in football made a Hitler joke and excused it by saying enough time had passed, Florio would've been among the first commentators to feign outrage.

Right after Dan Le Batard, of course.

DAN LE BATARD THINKS THERE ARE TOO MANY WHITE NFL ANALYSTS, DESPITE THE RACIAL MAKEUP OF HIS OWN COMPANY

That's the problem with too many of these sports media personalities. They try so hard to prove they're on the correct side of the culture war and sensitive to the right issues.

It's all so performative.

If Florio cared so much about DEI, as he claims, why did it take Jason Whitlock pointing out that he had never hired a black employee for him to hire one? Florio hired Myles Simmons, his first black employee, in 2020 after his exchange with Whitlock.

Likewise, if he were as accepting of everyone as he claims, why did it take Clay Travis calling attention to his past homophobic comments for him to acknowledge them?

"In the early days of PFT, we blended football news with attempts at humor. Some of those attempts at humor were offensive. I regret having made the comments, and I am sorry," Florio wrote in 2020, after accusing OutKick and Travis of insensitivity.

Florio understands that to exist in the mainstream sports media, he must conform to certain views. He isn't alone. Bill Simmons and Le Batard are the same way.

They appear ashamed of their frat-boy-ish pasts and feel compelled to overcompensate. It's the Howard Stern effect.

There are parallels between this behavior and several black commentators, who want to demonstrate they dislike white people as much as "Black Twitter" demands of them.

Jemele Hill and Mark Jones are not actually racist. Jones has a white spouse. They just want their followers and peers to think they are.

But every so often, these types of frauds let their guard down. That's what Florio did while discussing Vrabel's toothbrush mustache.

Next, he'll undoubtedly issue another apology explaining how sorry he is. He'll likely write another blog post calling for an NFL team to sign Kaepernick. Maybe he'll even call for the NFL to fund the first trans football league.

Mike Florio is a poser, by definition.

Finally, if an NFL insider is going to comment on Vrabel's mustache, we'd prefer one with more insight on the subject.

item.title: Boston College hockey to retire late Johnny Gaudreau's No 13 in pregame ceremony
item.description: Boston College will retire Johnny Gaudreau's No. 13 in Feb. 2027, honoring the 2014 Hobey Baker winner who led the Eagles to the 2012 national title.
item.content:encoded:
Boston College will retire the late Johnny Gaudreau’s No. 13 during a pregame ceremony on Feb. 12, 2027, the university announced Wednesday.

Gaudreau, nicknamed "Johnny Hockey," played at Boston College for three seasons (2011-14) and dominated during his tenure. He was a member of Boston College’s 2012 National Championship team as a freshman, led the nation in scoring as a junior and was awarded the 2014 Hobey Baker Award, which is presented to college hockey’s best player.

"We are proud to honor Johnny Gaudreau by retiring his No. 13 at Boston College," William V. Campbell Director of Athletics Blake James said in a statement. "Johnny was an extraordinary player who helped bring a national championship to the Heights and became one of the most accomplished players in our program's history. He will always hold a special place in the Boston College family."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

In three years with the Golden Eagles, Gaudreau had a whopping 175 points — 78 goals and 97 assists — in 119 games played. In 2013-14, Gaudreau had 80 points, which was the most of any college hockey player since Peter Sejna’s 82-point performance with Colorado College in 2002-03.

Gaudreau’s No. 13 is just the third number Boston College has retired, alongside David Emma’s No. 16 and Mike Mottau’s No. 3. The Calgary Flames drafted Gaudreau in the fourth round of the 2011 NHL Draft, and he made his debut with them at the end of the 2013-14 season.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

In his 11-year career, during which he spent nine seasons with the Flames and two with the Columbus Blue Jackets, he recorded 243 goals and 500 assists, good for 743 points in 763 games played.

Gaudreau and his brother Matthew, who played four seasons at Boston College, were tragically killed in 2024 in New Jersey, where they were visiting for their sister’s wedding. The brothers were riding their bicycles in Salem County, New Jersey, when Sean M. Higgins allegedly hit and killed them. Johnny was 31 and Matthew was 29 at the time of their deaths.

Higgins pleaded not guilty on Jan. 25 and is facing multiple charges, including two counts of aggravated manslaughter. He is slated to go to trial in January 2027 after he rejected a plea deal.

On Tuesday, it was announced that the childhood rink where the Gaudreaus played will have a bronze statue memorializing the brothers.

item.title: UConn's $32 million-plus Gampel Pavilion naming deal lands in court over a promise made in 1989
item.description: Harry A. Gampel's daughters allege UConn's $32.5 million M&T Bank deal broke a 1989 promise that his name would grace Gampel Pavilion in perpetuity.
item.content:encoded:
In 1989, Harry A. Gampel gave UConn $1 million to help build a basketball arena. The university’s president promised in writing that the building would bear Gampel’s name "in perpetuity."

Thirty-seven years later, three of Gampel’s daughters are suing over a 20-year naming deal with M&T Bank that CT Insider reported is worth $32.5 million. Margo Gampel Absher, Debra Gampel Fischman and Linda Gampel Abrahamson filed suit Nov. 11 in Hartford Superior Court against UConn’s Board of Trustees and the state of Connecticut.

The sisters allege the deal violates the terms of their father’s gift by giving the bank’s name more prominence on the building. They are asking a judge to order UConn to restore prominent exterior signage bearing the full name, Harry A. Gampel Pavilion.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Richard Weinstein, the family’s attorney, told OutKick in an email that his clients "are not looking for money." He said the family wants the arena called Harry A. Gampel Pavilion at M&T Bank Center, with both names displayed in lettering of the same size. Weinstein said he presented that exact proposal to UConn but received no response.

In a statement to OutKick, UConn said it "continues to honor and revere Harry A. Gampel, his extraordinary generosity, and his legacy." The university said it plans to add backlit signs recognizing Gampel at several public entrances, new signs inside the arena and a physical tribute to Gampel and the arena’s championship history.

The university also said it communicated with representatives of Gampel family members before the announcement and has sought in-person meetings with interested family members.

"Those invitations to meet have not yet been accepted," UConn said.

Weinstein told CT Insider the family is willing to meet to negotiate equal billing, but he disputed UConn’s account of its outreach.

In his Oct. 16, 1989, letter to Gampel, then-UConn President John T. Casteen III said the full name would appear on event tickets and in university publications, releases and public statements. He also described plans at the time for brass lettering above the southeast entrance and said the university would maintain signage identifying the building as Harry A. Gampel Pavilion for as long as it remained in service.

The arena opened in January 1990 and is the on-campus home of UConn’s men’s and women’s basketball teams. In a 2015 retrospective on the arena’s opening, UConn Athletics said the university had given Gampel "naming rights in perpetuity to the basketball arena."

It probably seemed like an easy decision at the time. Gampel’s gift was the largest private donation UConn had received. I doubt anyone in the president’s office was thinking about what a bank might pay to put its name on the same building 37 years later.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

On Oct. 21, trustees voted unanimously to authorize the name "M&T Bank Center at Harry A. Gampel Pavilion" for the larger athletics complex, which houses the arena and several offices. The authorization was contingent on a signed gift agreement. M&T’s announcement said the arena would be renamed "M&T Bank Center at Gampel Pavilion." That public name omits "Harry A." from the name the trustees authorized.

Photos show the M&T Bank Center lettering above the east entrance is much larger than the Gampel Pavilion lettering below it. In a letter reported by the Hartford Courant on Nov. 7, Gampel’s daughters said they would have accepted equal billing and said UConn had not consulted them.

Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont urged the family and the trustees to resolve the dispute in remarks reported Wednesday by CT Insider.

UConn athletic director David Benedict was talking about putting a corporate name next to Gampel’s as early as July 2025. UConn Athletics said in its 2026 annual report that it committed to sharing the full $20.5 million allowed in the 2025–26 revenue-sharing year. The limit for 2026–27 has since risen to $21.58 million. At the reported price, the M&T deal averages about $1.6 million a year.

I like stadium names that tell you something about the team or the city. Lambeau Field is named for a guy who helped start the Packers. Fenway Park is named for a part of Boston. Gampel Pavilion is named for a guy who helped get the place built. I’d take any of those names over whatever a sponsor is willing to put on a sign for the next 20 years.

I get why UConn took the deal. Keeping two championship-caliber rosters together in the NIL era is expensive.

But it doesn't mean I don't wish UConn had just left Gampel Pavilion alone.

item.title: Alzheimer’s blood marker could predict cognitive decline risks, Mayo Clinic says
item.description: A Mayo Clinic study finds a p-tau217 blood test may predict cognitive decline risk within five to 10 years, offering a less invasive option than PET scans.
item.content:encoded:
A blood test that detects a protein linked to Alzheimer’s disease could help predict whether older adults will develop cognitive decline within five to 10 years, according to a new Mayo Clinic study published in JAMA Neurology.

The study looked at levels of phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) in 2,178 cognitively unimpaired adults, ranging in age from 60 to 90. It also considered age, gender and whether participants carried the APOE ε4 genetic variant, which is associated with Alzheimer’s risk.

The participants, drawn from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging and the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, underwent blood biomarker testing, genetic testing and multiple cognitive assessments.

ALZHEIMER'S WARNING SIGNS COULD EMERGE YEARS BEFORE MEMORY LOSS, STUDY FINDS

While APOE ε4 had a modest association with risk after accounting for p-tau217, older age was associated with greater risk, according to the researchers.

For example, at the same elevated p-tau217 level, a 65-year-old faced a 6% estimated five-year risk of mild cognitive impairment, compared to a 37% risk for an 85-year-old.

Alzheimer’s disease is marked by plaques and tangles that accumulate in the brain, senior author Clifford Jack Jr., a Mayo Clinic neuroradiologist, noted. 

"The test tells you, just by taking a blood sample, whether someone has that pathology in the brain," he told Fox News Digital, adding higher levels of the pathology are associated with a greater risk of progressing from normal cognition to impairment.

10 HEALTH CONDITIONS MAY BE LINKED TO ALZHEIMER'S YEARS BEFORE DIAGNOSIS

Detecting p-tau217 in blood may be "less invasive and potentially more scalable" than using PET scans to measure amyloid burden, a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease that is associated with future cognitive impairment.

"The goal is to provide a personalized estimate of the risk of developing cognitive impairment that is more meaningful than simply reporting whether a blood test is positive or negative for amyloid pathology," first author Alicia Algeciras-Schimnich, Ph.D., a Mayo Clinic laboratory medicine and pathology researcher, said in a news release.

If investigational treatments are found to be effective at preventing or delaying cognitive decline, this blood test could take on greater significance, according to the researchers.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"If preventive treatments become available, this kind of information could help patients and clinicians have more informed conversations about the potential benefits and risks of treatment," Jack noted.

The risk estimates were developed in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging, which is drawn from a specific geographical area.

"The older population in southeast Minnesota is not representative of the entire United States," Jack said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

While the study’s methods could be applied to other populations, the researcher said the findings need to be replicated outside the region.

The risk prediction model is not yet ready for routine screening of people without cognitive symptoms, according to the research team.

"There is no treatment that’s been approved for people who are [asymptomatic] but have the disease in the brain," Jack told Fox News Digital. "Therefore, there’s no reason to do the test. … The results of the test would not change your medical management at all since there’s no treatment available."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

That could change if preventive treatments are approved, he added.

The study does not establish that routine blood testing prevents dementia or improves clinical outcomes.

"Many elderly people who have the pathology in the brain at lower levels will never develop symptoms in their lifetime," Jack added, noting that some people with Alzheimer’s-related pathology may also die of another cause before developing cognitive impairment.

item.title: US races to build bunkers across Middle East as Iranian strikes threaten American troops
item.description: The U.S. Army is hiring contractors to build 17 reinforced concrete bunkers in Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon amid Iranian missile and drone attacks.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Army is racing to hire contractors to build 17 reinforced concrete bunkers in Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon to protect American and coalition troops from deadly missile and drone attacks, according to a government procurement notice posted Friday.

The move comes amid escalating violence in the Middle East, where Iranian attacks on U.S. military installations have killed at least 23 American service members since war broke out in late February.

On Tuesday, Iran also claimed responsibility for another strike on a U.S. military base in Bahrain, its third attack there in five days.

BAHRAIN INTERCEPTS IRANIAN DRONES TARGETING US RADAR AFTER 2-MONTH LULL IN GULF STRIKES

Kuwaiti air defenses also intercepted incoming drones as Israeli forces launched new strikes in eastern and southern Lebanon.

The Army plans to build 10 bunkers in Israel, five in Saudi Arabia and two in Lebanon, replacing makeshift shelters made from shipping containers.

"Due to elevated regional force protection conditions, there is an urgent, high-priority requirement to replace nonstandard personnel protection shelters (e.g., converted shipping containers) and provide standardized, precast, reinforced concrete Indirect Fire bunkers," the Army said in the notice.

"The objective is to safeguard U.S. and coalition service members operating in potentially hostile environments across multiple countries in [U.S. Central Command] Area of Responsibility," the notice added.

PENTAGON JUMPS FROM $225M TO $55B ON DRONES AS CHEAP ATTACKS OVERWHELM US DEFENSES

The effort also follows a series of Iranian missile and drone attacks on U.S. bases across the Persian Gulf.

A March drone strike on a U.S. Army command post at Kuwait's Port of Shuaiba killed six American service members, with reports saying the facility lacked adequate protection against aerial attacks.

President Donald Trump said Nov. 16 that defensive measures had been effective across the region.

"Iran has fired between 8,000-9,000 One-way Attack Drones. Only 2 of them got through, resulting in U.S. fatalities, both on the first day, hitting Kuwait and Saudi Arabia. Likewise, Iran has fired about 2,000 Ballistic Missiles. Only 1 out of the 2,0000 got through, and caused U.S. fatalities (Jordan)," he wrote on Truth Social.

US CARRIES OUT SELF-DEFENSE STRIKE ON IRGC MISSILE LAUNCH SITE ON QESHM ISLAND

"Translation: 99.99% of Iranian missiles and drones have been shot down or, in any event, not caused U.S. deaths. [U.S. Central Command] defensive measures have been historically effective. No one in the World has the ability to do so well. All of this being left out of the 60 Minutes ‘report,’" he added.

The 17 bunkers will be built at five military installations: one in Israel and two each in Saudi Arabia and Lebanon, the notice said.

The Army is withholding the sites' locations for security reasons, saying names and coordinates will be provided only to eligible contractors once the formal solicitation is issued.

Each bunker will have three precast, reinforced concrete sections, steel entrance doors shielded by concrete barriers and sandbag-reinforced exterior walls.

Each roof will be covered with at least 18 inches of layered sandbags to protect against incoming fire.

US PULLS PERSONNEL FROM SAUDI ARABIA AS KINGDOM COMES UNDER HOUTHI FIRE

Contractors will have 45 days to finish construction after receiving a task order, while bidders will have just three days to submit quotes.

"Due to extreme operational urgency (soldiers currently at risk using non-standard containerized shelters), the subsequent solicitation is anticipated to have an expedited 3-day quote turnaround window," the Army said.

The Army is looking for construction and engineering firms that can deploy to Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon.

Contractors must respond by Nov. 25, and specify whether they can work in all three countries or only certain locations.

The Army is looking for "qualified, capable, and licensed construction and engineering firms with immediate cross-border and local mobilization capabilities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the State of Israel, and the Republic of Lebanon," the notice said.

The Pentagon and Army did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

item.title: Kim Jong Un's nuclear buildup sparks 'serious concern' ahead of Trump-Xi-Putin summit
item.description: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi warned Kim Jong Un's North Korean uranium enrichment expansion at Yongbyon is complete, calling it a serious concern.
item.content:encoded:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is accelerating his nuclear program, expanding a uranium enrichment facility that can produce plutonium for nuclear weapons, the United Nations' nuclear watchdog warned Wednesday, calling Pyongyang's growing program a "cause for serious concern."

International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Director General Rafael Grossi said the latest construction at the Yongbyon nuclear complex began in mid-September and was externally complete by late October, raising fresh alarms about North Korea's production of weapons-grade nuclear material.

"The ongoing expansion of the DPRK's uranium enrichment programme remains a cause for serious concern," Grossi said in remarks to the IAEA's board of governors in Vienna, referring to North Korea by its official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

TRUMP ARRIVES IN PHILIPPINES AHEAD OF XI JINPING SUMMIT IN CHINA AFTER GOP MIDTERM LOSSES

The warning came as President Donald Trump prepared to meet President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented three-way summit expected to address nuclear arms negotiations and other global security concerns.

Trump had also floated the possibility of meeting Kim during his trip to China, potentially opening another diplomatic channel with the North Korean dictator as Pyongyang continues to reject demands that it abandon its nuclear arsenal.

TRUMP CANNOT DETER XI AND PUTIN’S NUCLEAR GOALS WITH A STRATEGY DESIGNED FOR JUST ONE

As he departed the White House on Monday, Trump told reporters that denuclearization would be among the issues discussed with world leaders.

"We're going to talk about denuclearization – tough subject, because it's very hard for any of us to say we'll get rid of our nukes," Trump said.

The president also raised the possibility of Kim joining the diplomatic discussions, although no meeting with the North Korean leader has been confirmed.

"He may come. I don't know. That's up to President Xi," Trump told reporters. Trump also said he believed there was an opportunity for progress.

"So that'll be good. We have a chance to accomplish a lot," he added.

TRUMP TEASES POTENTIAL KIM JONG UN MEETING LATER THIS YEAR

The possibility of a meeting gained attention after Russia's Interfax news agency quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying Putin could meet Kim if the North Korean leader traveled to China for the summit, according to Reuters.

Trump said Tuesday that Kim would like to meet with him, adding, "We'll see what happens."

North Korea has repeatedly rejected calls to dismantle its nuclear weapons program, even as international monitors report continued construction and activity at key nuclear facilities.

Grossi said the IAEA had previously reported ongoing enrichment operations at Yongbyon and Kangson, construction of an additional enrichment facility at Yongbyon and indications of further expansion of North Korea's production of weapons-grade nuclear material.

"Since mid-September 2026, a further extension to the original Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction with the new extension externally complete by late-October 2026," Grossi said.

The agency also observed indications that Yongbyon's 5-megawatt reactor, which can produce plutonium for nuclear weapons, likely will continue to operate in its seventh irradiation cycle.

A separate light-water reactor at the complex resumed operations at the end of April following a shutdown, according to the agency.

NORTH KOREA MISSILE COULD PUT GUAM IN RANGE AS KIM REBUFFS TRUMP OUTREACH: EXPERT

"The continuation and further development of the DPRK's nuclear programme are clear violations of relevant UN Security Council resolutions and are deeply regrettable," Grossi said.

The IAEA has not had inspectors inside North Korea since 2009, when Pyongyang expelled them.

The agency now relies primarily on satellite imagery and other publicly available information to monitor nuclear developments, limiting its ability to independently verify activity inside the facilities.

North Korea carried out its first nuclear weapons test in 2006 and five additional tests through 2017, prompting successive rounds of U.N. Security Council sanctions targeting its nuclear and ballistic missile programs.

In September, IAEA member states also expressed "growing concern" over increased nuclear activity in North Korea, while Kim's sister, Kim Yo Jong, dismissed the pressure and said North Korea's status as a nuclear-armed country was "absolute" while calling those who continued to seek its denuclearization "idiots."

TRUMP REVEALS EXACT NUMBER OF NORTH KOREA'S NUCLEAR WEAPONS

Kim has also indicated that future talks with Washington would depend on the United States abandoning its demand for denuclearization and instead negotiating with North Korea as a nuclear-armed state.

The two leaders met in Singapore in 2018, when they signed a broad statement committing to work toward the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.

Their second summit, in Hanoi in 2019, ended without an agreement after negotiations broke down over North Korea's nuclear facilities and demands for sanctions relief.

Trump and Kim met again in June 2019 at the Demilitarized Zone separating North and South Korea, where Trump briefly crossed into North Korean territory.

Those meetings also failed to secure a verifiable agreement to dismantle North Korea's nuclear weapons program.
